newsitem.title: UK: Komercni's debut mark bond to be priced this week.
newsitem.headline: Komercni's debut mark bond to be priced this week.

text.p: A team from the Czech Republic's largest commercial bank, Komercni Banka a.s. -- in London ahead of the launch of the bank's debut mark Eurobond -- said the bond would be for 300 million marks, have a three-year maturity and a floating-rate coupon.
They said the bond was expected to be priced this week to yield in the low 20's basis points over three-month mark LIBOR. They said they would not swap the proceeds of the transaction.
"The primary objective of the mark bond is to have as broad a distribution as possible," Komercni Banka duputy chief executive Petr Budinsky said.
Merrill Lynch and Deutsche Bank AG were awarded the mandate to launch the mark bond earlier this month. The bank will raodshow in London and Frankfurt.

This transaction will be the second Eurobond issue for the bank. The first Eurobond was launched in April this year, a $250 million five-year bond -- the first Eurobond offered by any commercial bank in central and eastern europe.
It was priced to yield 78 b.p. over the yield on the five-year U.S. Treasury bond via C.S. First Boston and enjoyed wide demand.
Until then Komercni had tapped the syndicated loan markets.

In March, Komercni signed a 140 million mark three-year syndicated loan led by Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG. Komercni is rated Baa2 by Moody's Investors Service and is expected to be rated by Standard & Poor's Corp in October.
Budinsky said Komercni's strategy was to have access to all markets - the equity, syndicated loan, international capital and short-term debt markets - in order to repeatedly raise funds.

Komercni's financial markets managing director Lubor Zalman said the bank's objective was to be a sound and profitable bank: "According to western european criteria, not according to emerging markets criteria".
Budinsky said Komercni would also be interested in tapping the yen sector when the opportunity arose, but that the imminent mark bond would likely cover its financing needs for this year.
"But the demand is so high that it could change, it depends on (market) conditions," he said.
